original_text: 5.2 Application lifecycle [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.

attribute_scores.rationale: The terminology is generally clear within the ETSI MEC domain, though 'when required by the operator' is somewhat open to interpretation regarding trigger conditions.
Lacks specific inputs, parameters, and error handling for the instantiation process (e.g., resource exhaustion or invalid application packages).
Terminologies like 'MEC host', 'MEC management', and 'MEC system' are used consistently according to ETSI standards.
Uses the mandatory modal verb 'shall' appropriately, though it packages three separate tagged clauses ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) into a single requirement block.
Accurately reflects standard functional expectations for a telecommunications edge computing architecture.
The text actually combines three distinct requirements ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) into a single entry, violating the singularity rule.

While instantiating applications and checking host availability are testable, the vagueness of 'when required by the operator' makes verification of [Lifecycle-03] difficult without concrete input parameters.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.
shortcomings.explanation: The requirement text bundles three separate normative statements with individual tags ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) into one entry, violating the principle of singularity.
The condition 'when required by the operator' lacks specific trigger mechanisms, input parameters, or reference to interface protocols required to instantiate the application.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: The requirement belongs to an ETSI Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) specification focusing on application lifecycle management, specifically defining capabilities for MEC host availability and application instantiation by MEC management.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.
evaluations.context_reasoning: The requirement text explicitly embeds three separate tagged normative clauses ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) within a single requirement entry. This violates the engineering principle of singularity as these represent distinct testable capabilities.

In ETSI MEC architectural specifications, high-level functional requirements establish the capability for operator-triggered instantiation, while specific API schemas, parameters, and protocol bindings are delegated to companion interface specifications (e.g., Mp1, Mm1, Meao). Expecting complete interface parameters at this architectural overview stage is overly pedantic.

DEF-2 is discarded as a pedantic false positive since ETSI interface protocols and trigger mechanisms are defined in subsequent architectural and interface-specific clauses rather than high-level lifecycle requirements.
